summary: @servicetitan/time-zones ships obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes an undeclared obfuscated payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` is an obfuscated script (obfuscator.io-style `_0x...` identifier rotation and per-function string dictionaries hiding literals such as `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `bun`, `bun.exe`, and a GitHub release URL). At install time it probes for a local `bun` binary, otherwise downloads the Bun runtime zip from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...zip`, extracts `bun`/`bun.exe` into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and runs it via `execFileSync(bun, [path.join(D,'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`. The executed sibling `math_init.js` is a 728KB single-line file marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` with a shuffled numeric constant array and `_0x...` renamed identifiers; its filename does not match the declared purpose of the package (a React time-zones UI component library). `package.json` declares `"files": ["dist","src"]`, but neither `setup.mjs` nor `math_init.js` is listed in that manifest, yet both ship in the tarball. The composite behavior — obfuscated lifecycle script + off-manifest obfuscated blob + install-time fetch of an alternate runtime specifically to execute that blob outside Node's inspection surface — fires automatically on `npm install` with full installer privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
